svg.title: BCBC 2024 · 9.21.4.5 Lateral Stability
svg.text: BCBC 2024 · DIVISION B · PART 9 HOUSING AND SMALL BUILDINGS · SECTION 9.21 MASONRY AND CONCRETE CHIMNEYS AND FLUES
Lateral Stability

g.text: 600 × 450 mm, 3.0 m above the roof: no side
under 400 mm, not over 3.6 m high, (2)
450 × 450 mm, 4.2 m above the roof: over 3.6 m,
so brace to Subsection 4.3.2. for wind, (1)
Both (a) and (b) must be met for the exemption in Sentence (2). Height measured from the roof
to the top of the masonry in this example.

svg.text: WHAT THE CODE REQUIRES
Except as provided in Sentence (2), chimneys
are braced in accordance with Subsection
4.3.2. to provide lateral stability under wind
loads.
A chimney need not be laterally braced
provided
(a) no horizontal outside dimension is less than
400 mm (15¾″), and (b) the chimney extends not
more than 3.6 m (11′-9¾″) above a roof or the
masonry wall of which it forms a part.
Appendix note
A chimney fastened to the house framing with
metal anchors in accordance with CAN/CSA-A370,
"Connectors for masonry", is considered to have
adequate lateral support. The part above the roof
is considered free standing and may need more
lateral support.
Drawn: flat roofs so the height above the roof is plain. Subsection 4.3.2. is "Plain and Reinforced Masonry".
Source: BCBC 2024, Division B, Article 9.21.4.5. (page 9-160)
